items.statement: When the -l label-file option is used, calculations are limited to the specified label.
items.quote:
-l <label file>

limit calculations to specified label

items.statement: No flagged arguments are required.
items.quote:
Required Flagged Arguments

none

items.statement: Using -f requires either the -a or -l option to specify input.
items.quote:
-f <tablefile>

table output to tablefile (different format than -b). Must use -a or -l options to spec input.

items.statement: Input segmentation volume provided with --seg.
items.quote:
--seg segvol

input segmentation volume

items.statement: If an input volume is supplied, it must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.
items.quote: The input volume must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.

items.statement: If a mask volume is supplied, it must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.
items.quote: The mask volume must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.

items.statement: The FreeSurfer color table file maps each segmentation index to a segmentation name and color.
items.quote: Freesurfer color table file. Thi s the file used by FreeSurfer to specify how each segmentation index is mapped to a segmentation name and color.

items.statement: Partial volume compensation with --pv is usually only done when computing anatomical statistics and is not used with --annot.
items.quote:
--pv pvvol

Use pvvol to compenstate for partial voluming. This should result in more accurate volumes. Usually, this is only done when computing anatomical statistics. Usually the mri/norm.mgz volume is used. Not with --annot

items.statement: If no voxels meet the masking criteria, mri_segstats exits with an error.
items.quote: If no voxels meet the masking criteria, then mri_segstats exits with an error.

items.statement: If neither --id nor a color table is specified, all IDs from the segmentation volume are used.
items.quote: If the user does not specify either --id or a color table, then all the ids from the segmentation volume are used.

items.statement: If an input volume is supplied, it must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.
items.quote: The input volume must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.

items.statement: If a mask volume is supplied, it must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.
items.quote: The mask volume must be the same size and dimension as the segmentation volume.

items.statement: If no voxels meet the masking criteria, the program exits with an error.
items.quote: If no voxels meet the masking criteria, then mri_segstats exits with an error.

items.statement: With --meas surfmeasure, input is taken from subject/surf/hemi.surfmeasure.
items.quote:
--meas surfmeasure
Use subject/surf/hemi.surfmeasure as input.

items.statement: The --fsgd option specifies the input subject list from an FSGD file.
items.quote:
--fsgd fsgdfile
Specify the list of input subjects from the fsgd file.

items.statement: The registration matrix file is of the type accepted or created by tkregister2.
items.quote: The registration matrix file is of the type accepted/created by tkregister2.

items.statement: The --target option selects the common-space subject; --hemi selects lh or rh for source and target surfaces.
items.quote:
--target subject
Subject to use as the common-space. All the input data will be resampled to the surface of this subject.
--hemi hemi
Use hemi for source and target surfaces. hemi can be lh or rh.

items.statement: When subjects are listed using --s, each has its own --s; this option is for use with --meas.
items.quote:
--s subjN
Specify an input subject on the command-line. All subjects must be specified in this way on the command-line (ie, each with its own --s). For use with --meas.

items.statement: The --is option is an alternative to --meas and still requires a supplied subject list.
items.quote:
--is surfmeasfile
Specify full path to input surface measure file. This is an alternative to using --meas. This still requires that a subject list be supplied.

items.statement: For --paired-diff there must be an even number of inputs.
items.quote:
--paired-diff
After concatenating all the inputs together, create a new output file by computing paired differences, ie, Input1-Input2, Input3-Input4, etc. There must be an even number of inputs.

items.statement: When using full paths with --fsgd, subjects must be in the same order as the input surface files.
items.quote:
Same as #1 but using full paths. Note there is no --meas, but
--fsgd still needed to provide list of subjects, which must be in the same order as the --isp.

items.statement: --cache-out-only requires supplying a tmpdir.
items.quote: If you want to cache without actually creating an output, then --cache-out-only. You must supply a tmpdir.

items.statement: ANALYZE and NIFTI formats cannot represent a dimension with more than 32k elements.
items.quote: This will not work for ANALYZE and NIFTI formats because they cannot represent a dimension with more than 32k elements.

items.statement: None of the paired diff options will affect caching.
items.quote: None of the paired diff options will affect caching.

items.statement: Source subject name in $SUBJECTS_DIR or ico; input data must have been sampled onto this subject's surface.
items.quote: As found in $SUBJECTS_DIR or ico for icosahedron. The input data must have been sampled onto this subject's surface

items.statement: File containing the data on the source surface.
items.quote: Name of file where the data on the source surface is located.

items.statement: Target subject name in $SUBJECTS_DIR or ico for icosahedron.
items.quote: name of target subject as found in $SUBJECTS_DIR or ico for icosahedron.

items.statement: If source and target subjects differ, the registration surface is used; sphere.reg is the default.
items.quote: If the source and target subjects are not the same, this surface is used to register the two surfaces. sphere.reg is used as the default.

items.statement: For trg_type w or paint, use the full path for the target file.
items.quote: BUG ALERT: for trg_type w or paint, use the full path.

items.statement: With paint output, specify the output file with a partial path or it will be written into the subject's anatomical directory.
items.quote: When the output format is paint, the output file must be specified with a partial path (eg, ./data-lh.w) or else the output will be written into the subject's anatomical directory.

items.statement: The metric file to resample, typically a native-mesh metric.
items.quote: <metric-in> - the metric file to resample, typically a native-mesh metric

items.statement: A sphere surface in register with the new sphere and having the mesh the metric is currently on.
items.quote:
<current-sphere> - a sphere surface that is in register with <new-sphere>
and has the mesh that the metric is currently on, typically a
registered native-mesh sphere

items.statement: A sphere surface that is the desired output mesh, typically a standard sphere.
items.quote:
<new-sphere> - a sphere surface that the desired output mesh, typically a
standard sphere

items.statement: The method argument must be one of ADAP_BARY_AREA or BARYCENTRIC.
items.quote:
The <method> argument must be one of the following:

ADAP_BARY_AREA
BARYCENTRIC

items.statement: If ADAP_BARY_AREA is used, exactly one of -area-surfs or -area-metrics must be specified.
items.quote:
If ADAP_BARY_AREA is used, exactly one of -area-surfs or
-area-metrics must be specified.

items.statement: The current sphere must be in register with the new sphere.
items.quote: <current-sphere> - a sphere surface that is in register with <new-sphere>

items.statement: The -current-roi option only masks the input; the output may be slightly dilated in comparison.
items.quote:
The -current-roi option only masks the input, the output may be slightly
dilated in comparison

items.statement: The anatomical input is a structural intensity image, typically T1.
items.quote: Structural *intensity* image, typically T1.

items.statement: Brain segmentation template: an anatomical intensity template that is not skull-stripped.
items.quote: Anatomical *intensity* template. This template is *not* skull-stripped.

items.statement: Brain extraction probability mask in the segmentation template space; a binary mask is acceptable.
items.quote:
Brain *probability* mask in the segmentation template space. A binary mask
                                                is an acceptable probability image.

items.statement: At least four priors must exist, corresponding to CSF, cortical GM, WM and subcortical GM.
items.quote: At least four priors must exist, corresponding to CSF, Cortical GM, WM, Subcortical GM.

items.statement: Image dimension must be 2 or 3.
items.quote: ImageDimension must be 2 or 3

items.statement: If a registration template is supplied with -t, it must be skull-stripped.
items.quote: -t:  template for t1 registration          Anatomical *intensity* template. This template *must* be skull-stripped.

items.statement: If an extraction registration mask is supplied with -f, it is a binary metric mask in the segmentation template space (-e).
items.quote: -f:  extraction registration mask          Binary metric mask defined in the segmentation template space (-e).

items.statement: At least four prior images are required; fewer causes the script to exit.
items.quote:
if [[ ${NUMBER_OF_PRIOR_IMAGES} -lt 4 ]]; then
  echo "Expected at least 4 prior images (${NUMBER_OF_PRIOR_IMAGES} are specified).  Check the command line specification."
  exit 1
fi

items.statement: The segmentation template and registration template may be different.
items.quote: the segmentation template (used for brain extraction and priors) and registration template (used for final, high-quality registration on brain-extracted images) may be different

items.statement: If command -v cannot find a dependency program, the script reports an error.
items.quote:
if ! command -v ${D} &> /dev/null
      then
        echo "Error:  we can't find the $D program."

items.statement: Specified anatomical images are checked for existence.
items.quote:
if [[ ! -f ${ANATOMICAL_IMAGES[$i]} ]];
    then
      echo "The specified image \"${ANATOMICAL_IMAGES[$i]}\" does not exist."
      exit 1
    fi

items.statement: The script tests each expected output image for existence and records missing outputs.
items.quote:
for img in "${singleOutputs[@]}";
    do
      if [[ ! -f $img ]];
        then
          echo "Missing output image $img"
          missingOutput=1
        fi

items.statement: The script checks for the affine registration transform from the segmentation step.
If a command exits with nonzero status, the script exits unless debug mode is enabled.
items.quote:
ERROR: command exited with nonzero status $cmdExit"
      echo "Command: $cmd"
      echo
      if [[ ! $DEBUG_MODE -gt 0 ]];
        then
          exit 1
        fi

items.statement: For Templateflow priors, if SGM is not found then SCGM is used instead.
items.quote:
Templateflow labels use "SCGM" instead of "SGM", if "SGM" is not
                                                found, "SCGM" will be used instead.

items.statement: Prior combinations are only allowed for gray matter or white matter; other labels cause an error exit.
items.quote:
We only combine with the gray matter or the white matter."
        echo "The label ${COMBINATION[0]} does not correspond to the gray or white matters."
        exit 1

items.statement: If the cortical thickness output is not produced, the script exits with an error.
items.quote:
if [[ ! -f ${CORTICAL_THICKNESS_IMAGE} ]];
      then
        echo "Expected output was not produced.  The cortical thickness image doesn't exist:"
        echo "   $CORTICAL_THICKNESS_IMAGE"
        exit 1
      fi

specify classifier array input file

and uses the mesh that the input surface is currently on, typically a

items.statement: The method name, which must be one of ADAP_BARY_AREA or BARYCENTRIC.
items.quote:
The <method> argument must be one of the following:

ADAP_BARY_AREA
BARYCENTRIC

items.statement: If ADAP_BARY_AREA is used, exactly one of -area-surfs or -area-metrics must be specified.
items.quote:
If ADAP_BARY_AREA is used, exactly one of -area-surfs or
-area-metrics must be specified.

items.statement: For cut surfaces (including flatmaps), use -surface-cut-resample instead.
items.quote: For cut surfaces (including flatmaps), use -surface-cut-resample.

items.statement: Instead of resampling a spherical surface, the -surface-sphere-project-unproject command is recommended.
items.quote:
Instead of resampling a spherical surface, the
-surface-sphere-project-unproject command is recommended.

items.statement: ADAP_BARY_AREA is not generally recommended for surface resampling, but is provided for completeness.
items.quote:
If ADAP_BARY_AREA is used, exactly one of -area-surfs or
-area-metrics must be specified. This method is not generally
recommended for surface resampling, but is provided for completeness.

items.statement: FIRST needs a good quality T1-weighted image.
items.quote: FIRST needs a good quality T1-weighted image

items.statement: Only T1-weighted images can be used as input to run_first_all.
items.quote:
run_first_all -i t1_image -o output_name

The argument -i specifies the original T1-weighted structural image (only T1-weighted images can be used).

items.statement: first_flirt should be used on whole-head (non-betted) images.
items.quote: first_flirt should be used on whole-head (non-betted) images

items.statement: If the registration stage fails then the model fitting will not work, though run_first_all continues to run and may produce outputs.
items.quote:
if the registration stage fails then the models fitting will
not work, despite the fact that run_first_all continues to run and may produce outputs.

items.statement: When fitting the cerebellum models, a different transformation matrix than that used for the other structures must be input.
items.quote: When fitting the cerebellum models, you will need to input a different transformation matrix than that used for the other structures.

items.statement: The -cort flag must be specified for first_flirt to perform the registration needed for cerebellum models.
items.quote: cerebellum models, you will need to input a different transformation matrix than that used for the other structures. first_flirt will not perform the necessary registration by default - the -cort flag must be specified.

items.statement: The full path name to the model must be used with -m.
items.quote: -m: The model file (e.g. ${FSLDIR}/data/first/models_336_bin/L_Hipp_bin.bmv). The full path name to the model must be used.

items.statement: Check the log directory error outputs; no output means no errors.
items.quote:
cat *.logs/*.e*

and if there are no errors then you will see no output, otherwise you will see what errors have occured.

items.statement: Check registration quality using slicesdir on the registered images.
items.quote: slicesdir -p ${FSLDIR}/data/standard/MNI152_T1_1mm.nii.gz *_to_std_sub.nii.gz

items.statement: Pay particular attention to the sub-cortical structures when assessing registrations.
items.quote: pay particular attention to the sub-cortical structures

items.statement: Check segmentation quality with first_roi_slicesdir, which generates a webpage summary.
items.quote: first_roi_slicesdir is a script to generate summary images, in a webpage format, for the segmentation outputs

items.statement: If there are problems, different segmentation options such as number of modes or boundary correction method can be tried using the individual tools.
items.quote: If there are any problems, you can try different segmentation options (e.g. number of modes, boundary correction method, etc.) using the individual tools described in the Advanced Usage section.

items.statement: Boundary correction method none is appropriate for models in the 05mm subdirectory.
items.quote: For the models contained in ${FSLDIR}/data/first/models_336_bin/05mm/, all boundary voxels are considered as belonging to the structure, and hence none is the appropriate correction method.
